# Task 00 — CI, Branch Protection & Auto-merge

> Read `build/prompts/_shared-context.md` first.

## Objective
Establish repository readiness for the pipeline: a GitHub Actions `ci-gate` workflow, branch protection on `main`, a correct `.gitignore`, and repo scaffolding so every subsequent task's PR is gated and auto-mergeable. This is the safety net for all later tasks.

## Context
The AFDT pipeline creates one branch + PR per task and relies on a green `ci-gate` check + auto-merge to land work without stacking (see `docs/build-pipeline-pattern.md`). This task must exist and pass BEFORE any feature work, or PRs stack unmerged. There is no app code yet — the workflow must be tolerant of an early/empty project but wired to run the real gates once T01 lands package.json scripts.

## Technical Requirements
1. Create `.gitignore` including at minimum: `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `.env`, `.env.*` (but keep `.env.example`), `ios/App/Pods/`, `android/.gradle/`, `*.log`, `.DS_Store`, coverage/, playwright-report/, test-results/.
2. Create `.github/workflows/ci-gate.yml`:
   - Trigger on `pull_request` to `main` and `workflow_dispatch`.
   - Job `ci-gate` on `ubuntu-latest`, Node 20, `npm ci` (fallback `npm install` if no lockfile yet).
   - Steps run only if the script exists (guard with `npm run <x> --if-present`): `lint`, `typecheck`, `build`, `test`.
   - Must succeed on an empty/early repo (so T00's own PR is green) yet enforce the gates once scripts exist.
3. Add `.env.example` documenting required vars (no secrets): `VITE_SUPABASE_URL`, `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `VITE_SENTRY_DSN`, `VITE_APP_ENV` (dev|staging|prod).
4. Add `README.md` stub: project name, stack, "backend lives in Supabase `app` schema (already built)", how to run, link to BUILD-PLAN.
5. Ensure the default branch is `main`; this workflow's check name is exactly `ci-gate` (branch protection depends on it).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `.github/workflows/ci-gate.yml` exists; the check id is `ci-gate`.
- [ ] Workflow passes on this task's own PR (empty-project tolerant via `--if-present`).
- [ ] `.gitignore` excludes `node_modules/`, `.env`, build/native artifacts; `.env.example` is committed.
- [ ] `README.md` + `.env.example` present and accurate.
- [ ] No secrets committed anywhere.

## Constraints
- Do NOT hardcode any Supabase URL/key. Do NOT create app source beyond README/env example.
- Keep the workflow resilient to missing scripts (use `--if-present`).

## Dependencies
- None (first task).

## Files Expected
- `.gitignore`
- `.github/workflows/ci-gate.yml`
- `.env.example`
- `README.md`

# Task 01 — Project Scaffold (Vite + React + TS + Capacitor)

> Read `build/prompts/_shared-context.md` first.

## Objective
Scaffold the application: Vite + React 18 + TypeScript, Capacitor 6 native shell (iOS + Android targets), ESLint + Prettier, a clean feature-first folder structure, and the npm scripts the CI gate expects. This is the foundation every other task builds on.

## Context
Stack is fixed (see shared context): React 18.3, TypeScript 5.5, Vite 5, Capacitor 6, React Router 6, Recharts, MapLibre GL, lucide-react. Mobile-first. The backend is the live Supabase `app` schema — this task creates NO backend and NO DB types yet (that is T02).

## Technical Requirements
1. Initialize Vite React-TS app at repo root. React 18.3, TypeScript 5.5, strict mode on in `tsconfig`.
2. Add dependencies: `react-router-dom@6`, `@supabase/supabase-js@2`, `recharts`, `maplibre-gl`, `lucide-react`, `@capacitor/core@6`, `@capacitor/cli@6`, `@capacitor/ios@6`, `@capacitor/android@6`, plus dev: `eslint`, `prettier`, `eslint-config-prettier`, `typescript`, `vitest`, `@playwright/test`.
3. npm scripts: `dev`, `build` (`tsc -b && vite build`), `preview`, `lint` (eslint), `typecheck` (`tsc -b --noEmit` or `tsc --noEmit`), `test` (vitest run), `test:e2e` (playwright). These names must match T00's CI gate.
4. `capacitor.config.ts`: appId `com.tnfg.nofaultapp3` (confirm naming), appName "No Fault App 3.0", webDir `dist`. Add iOS + Android platforms (`npx cap add ios`, `npx cap add android`) — scaffold configs; do not require a Mac to build here.
5. Folder structure (feature-first):
   ```
   src/
     app/            # app entry, router, providers
     components/     # shared UI primitives (T03 fills these)
     features/       # feature modules (leads, auth, charts, portals, ...)
     lib/            # supabase client, queries, validation, constants, types
     pages/          # route-level pages
     styles/         # theme tokens, globals
   ```
6. ESLint + Prettier configured and passing on the scaffold. Set up `src/app/App.tsx` with a minimal router and a placeholder route so `build` succeeds.
7. `.env` plumbing: read `import.meta.env.VITE_*`; add a tiny `src/lib/env.ts` that validates required vars at startup and throws a clear error if missing (no hardcoded values).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `npm install`, `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` all pass.
- [ ] Capacitor configured with iOS + Android platforms; `capacitor.config.ts` correct.
- [ ] Folder structure created as specified; strict TS on.
- [ ] `src/lib/env.ts` validates `VITE_SUPABASE_URL`/`VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` presence.
- [ ] App boots to a placeholder route in `vite preview`.

## Constraints
- No backend/DB types here (T02). No hardcoded secrets. Keep dependencies to the fixed stack; do not introduce a different router/state/UI library.

## Dependencies
- T00 (CI gate + gitignore).

## Files Expected
- `package.json`, `tsconfig*.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `.eslintrc*`, `.prettierrc`
- `capacitor.config.ts`, `ios/`, `android/` (scaffold)
- `src/app/App.tsx`, `src/app/router.tsx`, `src/lib/env.ts`, `index.html`

tasks.description:
# Task 02 — Supabase Client + Generated `app`-schema Types

> Read `build/prompts/_shared-context.md` first.

## Objective
Wire the Supabase client and generate TypeScript types directly from the live `app` schema. This establishes the typed data contract for the entire app and is the #1 drift-prevention control — no hand-written DB types anywhere.

## Context
The backend is the live `app` schema (58 tables, RLS, rule-engine functions). App 2.0 suffered four deployed-vs-code drift bugs from hand-written types; App 3.0 forbids that. The Supabase client must target the `app` schema and pass the user JWT so RLS applies.

## Technical Requirements
1. Create `src/lib/supabase.ts` exporting a typed client:
   - `createClient<Database>(url, anonKey, { db: { schema: 'app' }, auth: { persistSession: true, autoRefreshToken: true } })`.
   - URL/key from `import.meta.env` via `src/lib/env.ts`. Never hardcode.
2. Generate types: add a script `gen:types` → `supabase gen types typescript --project-id <PROJECT_ID from env/CI> --schema app > src/lib/database.types.ts`. Commit a generated `database.types.ts` covering the `app` schema (tables, enums, functions). Document the regen command in README.
   - The generated `Database` type MUST include the `app` schema tables and the callable functions (`fn_cnv_value`, `fn_log_status`, `visible_lead_ids`, `visible_user_ids`, `current_portal_kind`, `is_admin`).
3. Add typed helpers in `src/lib/db.ts`:
   - `type Tables<T> = Database['app']['Tables'][T]['Row']` and Insert/Update equivalents.
   - Export handy row aliases: `AppUser`, `Lead`, `LeadLegal`, `LeadClinical`, `Client`, `RefAttorney`, `RefTxLocation`, etc. NOTE the three quoted camelCase tables map to keys `refLeadStatus`/`refClinicalStatus`/`refLegalStatus` in the generated types — alias them cleanly.
4. Environment separation: support dev/staging/prod via `VITE_APP_ENV` + per-env `VITE_SUPABASE_URL`/`_ANON_KEY`. Provide `.env.example` entries and a short README section. No secrets committed.
5. Add a `src/lib/rpc.ts` with thin typed wrappers for the rule-engine + visibility functions (e.g. `getCnvValue(idLead)`, `getLogStatus(idLead)`), calling `supabase.rpc('fn_cnv_value', { p_id_lead })` etc.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/lib/database.types.ts` is generated from the `app` schema and committed; NO hand-written table interfaces exist in the codebase.
- [ ] `src/lib/supabase.ts` targets `schema: 'app'`, persists session, passes JWT (RLS-ready).
- [ ] `src/lib/rpc.ts` typed wrappers compile against generated function types.
- [ ] dev/staging/prod env separation documented and env-driven; no hardcoded URL/key.
- [ ] `npm run typecheck` passes with the generated types in use.

## Constraints
- Do NOT hand-write any table/row types. Do NOT alter the schema. Do NOT commit real keys.
- If `supabase gen types` cannot reach the project in CI, commit a checked-in generated file and document the regen step; keep the committed file authoritative.

## Dependencies
- T01 (scaffold + env).

## Files Expected
- `src/lib/supabase.ts`, `src/lib/database.types.ts`, `src/lib/db.ts`, `src/lib/rpc.ts`
- `.env.example` (updated), README section on type regen + envs

# Task 03 — Design System

> Read `build/prompts/_shared-context.md` first.

## Objective
Build the App-3.0 design system: theme tokens and a set of mobile-first, accessible base components that every screen composes from — carrying forward the App-2.0 visual language (teal, cards, donut+table charts, bottom-sheet filters).

## Context
Design language (App 2.0, see shared context §Design system): primary teal/cyan `#00BCD4`; light-gray cards `#F5F5F5`; success green, alert red/pink; rounded corners; bold-teal section headers; small uppercase teal labels. Charts are donut/ring + data table underneath. Filters are bottom-sheet modals with "Clear all"/"Done". Persistent bottom nav + hamburger menu.

## Technical Requirements
1. `src/styles/theme.ts` — design tokens: colors (primary `#00BCD4`, card `#F5F5F5`, success, danger, warning, purple/yellow for log-status GREEN/RED/PURPLE/YELLOW/WHITE), spacing scale, radius, typography, shadows. Export a typed `theme` object + CSS variables in `src/styles/globals.css`.
2. Base components in `src/components/` (typed props, accessible, mobile-first, keyboard + screen-reader friendly):
   - `Button` (primary teal-filled / outline / ghost / danger; loading state)
   - `Input`, `TextArea`, `Select` (labelled, error state, helper text)
   - `PillToggle` (single + multi-select pills — used for boosted?/language/yes-no)
   - `Card`, `SectionHeader` (bold teal), `Badge`/`StatusBadge` (maps a log-status code→color)
   - `Modal` + `BottomSheet` (the filter modal pattern: title, body, "Clear all" + "Done")
   - `Avatar`, `EmptyState`, `LoadingState`, `ErrorState`, `Chevron`/list-row primitives
   - `DonutChart` + `DataTable` pair (Recharts donut with center total + teal gradient by rank; table sorted desc, alternating rows) — the reusable chart widget every dashboard uses
3. `StatusBadge` must accept a log-status code (`GREEN|RED|PURPLE|YELLOW|WHITE`) and render the matching color + label; source the mapping from `app.ref_log_status` where practical (or a typed constant kept in sync).
4. Storybook is NOT required; instead add a `/dev/components` route (dev-only) that renders every component for visual QA.
5. All interactive components: focus states, `aria-*`, 44px min tap targets, color-contrast AA.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Theme tokens + CSS variables exist; teal `#00BCD4` primary applied.
- [ ] All listed base components implemented, typed, and accessible (focus/aria/tap-target).
- [ ] `DonutChart`+`DataTable` renders a donut with center total + a sorted table underneath.
- [ ] `StatusBadge` maps all five log-status codes to correct colors/labels.
- [ ] `/dev/components` shows the full component gallery; `build`/`typecheck`/`lint` pass.

## Constraints
- No third-party component kit (build on the fixed stack + lucide-react icons). Keep it mobile-first. Do not fetch data in components — presentational only.

## Dependencies
- T01 (scaffold).

## Files Expected
- `src/styles/theme.ts`, `src/styles/globals.css`
- `src/components/*` (all components above, one file each + `index.ts`)
- `src/pages/dev/ComponentsGallery.tsx`

tasks.name: Sentry + Error Handling
tasks.description:
# Task 04 — Sentry + Error Handling

> Read `build/prompts/_shared-context.md` first.

## Objective
Wire Sentry error tracking and a consistent error-handling pattern early, so no error is ever silently swallowed. App 2.0 had invisible errors until a `describeError` helper was added mid-build; App 3.0 does this up front (premium-bar item).

## Context
Premium production bar requires observability. Every data call, mutation, and async boundary must route failures to a shared handler; no empty `catch {}`.

## Technical Requirements
1. Add `@sentry/react`. Initialize in `src/lib/sentry.ts` from `VITE_SENTRY_DSN` + `VITE_APP_ENV` (skip init cleanly if DSN absent, e.g. local dev). Set environment, release, and `tracesSampleRate` sensibly per env.
2. Wrap the app in a Sentry `ErrorBoundary` (in `src/app/App.tsx`) with a friendly fallback UI (reuse `ErrorState` from T03).
3. Create `src/lib/errors.ts`:
   - `captureError(err, context?)` — logs to console in dev, reports to Sentry in staging/prod, returns a normalized `AppError` `{ message, code?, cause? }`.
   - `describeError(err)` — human-readable message extractor (handles Supabase `PostgrestError`, network errors, thrown strings).
4. Establish the convention (documented in README + a code comment): all `lib/queries/*` and mutations use `try/catch` → `captureError` → rethrow a normalized error the UI can show. No silent catches anywhere.
5. Add a dev-only "throw test error" button on `/dev/components` to verify boundary + Sentry path.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Sentry initializes from env; no-DSN case degrades gracefully (no crash).
- [ ] App wrapped in an ErrorBoundary with a friendly fallback.
- [ ] `captureError`/`describeError` implemented and exported; handle `PostgrestError`.
- [ ] Convention documented; no empty `catch {}` in the codebase (lint/grep clean).
- [ ] `build`/`typecheck`/`lint` pass.

## Constraints
- Never log secrets/PII to Sentry. Do not hardcode the DSN. Keep dev noise low (console in dev, Sentry in staging/prod).

## Dependencies
- T01 (scaffold). Uses T03 `ErrorState` if available (soft).

## Files Expected
- `src/lib/sentry.ts`, `src/lib/errors.ts`
- `src/app/App.tsx` (ErrorBoundary wiring)
- README section on error-handling convention

tasks.description:
# Task 05 — Auth (Email-OTP + `app_user` Resolution)

> Read `build/prompts/_shared-context.md` first.

## Objective
Implement authentication: Supabase Auth email-OTP login, session persistence, and resolution of the signed-in `auth.uid()` to the correct `app.app_user` row — exposing the user's `portal_kind` (EMPLOYEE/ATTORNEY/AFFILIATE/ADMIN) to the whole app. This is the gateway to the three-audience model.

## Context
Attorneys and affiliates are EXTERNAL (no Google Workspace) — so identity is Supabase Auth (email + OTP), NOT SSO. After login, the app must look up `app_user WHERE auth_user_id = auth.uid()`; that row's `portal_kind` drives all routing/visibility (T06). RLS depends on the JWT being attached (handled by the Supabase client from T02).

## Technical Requirements
1. Auth screens in `src/features/auth/`:
   - `LoginPage` — email input → `supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({ email })` (magic-link/OTP). Branded (305/TNFG, dark theme per 2.0 login).
   - `OtpVerifyPage` (or same page step 2) — enter the emailed code → `supabase.auth.verifyOtp(...)`. Handle the redirect/callback if using magic link.
2. Session: rely on the T02 client's `persistSession`/`autoRefreshToken`. Add `src/features/auth/AuthProvider.tsx` (React context) exposing `{ session, appUser, portalKind, loading, signOut }`.
3. **`app_user` resolution:** on session established, query `app.app_user` for `auth_user_id = session.user.id` (RLS allows self-select). Store the row + `portal_kind` in context. If no `app_user` row exists for the email, show a clear "account not provisioned" state (do NOT auto-create).
4. `useAuth()` hook + `useAppUser()`/`usePortalKind()` selectors.
5. Route guard primitive `RequireAuth` (redirects to login when no session) — the audience-specific guards come in T06.
6. Sign-out clears session + context and returns to login.
7. Errors via T04 `captureError`; friendly messages via `describeError`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Email-OTP login + verify works end-to-end against Supabase Auth; session persists across reload.
- [ ] After login, the matching `app.app_user` row is resolved and `portal_kind` is available app-wide via context.
- [ ] Unprovisioned email (no `app_user`) shows a clear non-crashing state; no auto-provisioning.
- [ ] `RequireAuth` redirects unauthenticated users to login.
- [ ] Sign-out fully clears state. `build`/`typecheck`/`lint` pass.

## Constraints
- No passwords (OTP only). Do NOT create `app_user` rows from the client. Trust RLS for the self-select. No PII in logs.

## Dependencies
- T02 (client + types).

## Files Expected
- `src/features/auth/LoginPage.tsx`, `OtpVerifyPage.tsx`, `AuthProvider.tsx`, `useAuth.ts`
- `src/features/auth/RequireAuth.tsx`
- `src/lib/queries/appUser.ts` (self-resolve query)

tasks.description:
# Task 06 — App Shell (portal_kind Branching + Nav + Guards)

> Read `build/prompts/_shared-context.md` first.

## Objective
Build the application shell that branches the entire experience on `portal_kind`: the persistent bottom navigation, the hamburger menu, and audience-specific route guards so employees, attorneys, affiliates, and admins each see only their surface.

## Context
One app, three audiences (+ admin). `portal_kind` comes from the `app_user` row resolved in T05. Employees get the full 2.0-style surface (Home, leads, mapper, directory, request portal, charts). Attorneys get the Attorney Portal (T20). Affiliates get the Affiliate Portal (T21). Admin gets everything + settings. Bottom nav + hamburger are the 2.0 navigation pattern.

## Technical Requirements
1. `src/app/AppShell.tsx` — top-level authenticated layout: renders bottom nav + hamburger + `<Outlet/>`. Reads `portalKind` from `useAuth()`.
2. **Bottom nav** — audience-aware tabs:
   - EMPLOYEE/ADMIN: Home · (Leads) · Mapper (globe) — mirror 2.0's Home/Scheduling(deactivated→omit or replace)/Mapper; use Home / Leads / Mapper.
   - ATTORNEY: Home(portal) · Leads · (no Mapper).
   - AFFILIATE: Home(portal) · Leads/Appointments.
3. **Hamburger menu** — audience-aware items:
   - EMPLOYEE: 1800 Directory, Request Portal, Human Resources, Dashboards. (Atty & AFF Settings only for ADMIN/IT.)
   - ATTORNEY/AFFILIATE: minimal (Profile, Sign out, portal-relevant links).
   - ADMIN: all of the above + Atty & AFF Settings + `/dev/components` (dev).
4. **Route guards**: `RequirePortal({ allow: PortalKind[] })` wrapping route groups; unauthorized access redirects to the user's home surface (not a raw 403). Compose with `RequireAuth` (T05).
5. `src/app/router.tsx` — define the route tree with lazy-loaded route groups per audience; wire placeholders for pages built in later tasks so the shell compiles and navigates now.
6. Header/user-profile footer in the hamburger (avatar, name, email, sign-out) per 2.0.
7. Respect safe areas / notches (Capacitor); bottom nav above the home indicator.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Shell renders and branches nav + menu correctly for each `portal_kind` (EMPLOYEE/ATTORNEY/AFFILIATE/ADMIN).
- [ ] `RequirePortal` blocks cross-audience routes and redirects to the user's own home.
- [ ] Bottom nav + hamburger match the audience matrix above; sign-out works from the menu.
- [ ] Router tree defined with lazy route groups + placeholders; navigation works.
- [ ] Safe-area handling correct on device viewport. `build`/`typecheck`/`lint` pass.

## Constraints
- Do not duplicate RLS logic — `portal_kind` drives UI/routing; row security is server-side. Keep placeholders minimal; real pages come later. No audience should see another's nav items.

## Dependencies
- T03 (components), T05 (auth + portalKind).

## Files Expected
- `src/app/AppShell.tsx`, `src/app/router.tsx`
- `src/components/nav/BottomNav.tsx`, `HamburgerMenu.tsx`
- `src/features/auth/RequirePortal.tsx`

tasks.name: Lead Query/Data Layer (+ rule-engine RPCs)
tasks.description:
# Task 07 — Lead Query/Data Layer (+ Rule-Engine RPCs)

> Read `build/prompts/_shared-context.md` first.

## Objective
Build the typed data-access layer for the lead domain: reads/writes against the `app` schema tables and RPC wrappers for the live rule-engine + visibility functions. Every screen consumes this layer — it centralizes queries so UI never issues ad-hoc SQL and never recomputes business rules.

## Context
Lead is the hub with 1:1 summaries + 1:M details (see shared context). RLS already scopes rows to the caller's audience. CNV and log-status are LIVE functions (`fn_cnv_value`, `fn_log_status`) — call them, never reimplement. Types come from the generated `database.types.ts` (T02).

## Technical Requirements
1. `src/lib/queries/leads.ts`:
   - `listLeads(params)` — paginated lead list with joins to `refLeadStatus` (status label/icon), submitter (`app_user`), primary client (via `lead_party`+`client`), and log-status. Support status filter, search (name/phone), and standard filters (office/pod/team) as passthrough — RLS already limits scope.
   - `getLead(idLead)` — full aggregate: `lead` + `lead_accident` + `lead_clinical` (+ `ref_tx_location`) + `lead_legal` (+ `ref_attorney`, `refLegalStatus`) + `lead_timeline` + `lead_party`(+client) + `lead_injury`/`lead_injury_site` + `lead_insurance` + `lead_note` + `lead_status_event`.
   - `createLead(input)`, `updateLead(idLead, patch)`, and section updaters (`upsertLeadClinical`, `upsertLeadLegal`, etc.).
2. `src/lib/queries/clients.ts` — `findClientByPhone`, `createClient`, address/channel helpers.
3. `src/lib/rpc.ts` (extend T02): `getCnvValue(idLead)`, `getLogStatus(idLead)`, `getVisibleLeadIds()`, `getVisibleUserIds()`, `currentPortalKind()`, `isAdmin()` — typed against generated function signatures.
4. `src/lib/queries/refData.ts` — cached loaders for dropdown catalogs: states, `refLeadStatus`, `refLegalStatus`, `refClinicalStatus`, `ref_attorney`, `ref_tx_location`, `ref_insurance_carrier`, `ref_injury_site`, `ref_severity_level`, `party_kind`, `staff_kind`, `ref_lead_stage`. Reference the three camelCase tables with their exact quoted keys from generated types.
5. All functions: typed inputs/outputs (from generated types), `captureError` on failure (T04), no silent catches. Use a small query-key convention if adding React Query (optional — plain async is fine, but be consistent).
6. Do NOT add client-side row filtering that duplicates RLS; you MAY add UX filters (status tab, search).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `getLead` returns a fully-typed aggregate spanning lead + all 1:1 and 1:M related tables.
- [ ] `listLeads` supports pagination + status/search filters and returns status label + log-status.
- [ ] RPC wrappers call `fn_cnv_value`/`fn_log_status`/`visible_lead_ids` and are typed from generated function types — CNV/log-status are NEVER computed in JS.
- [ ] Ref-data loaders cover all dropdown catalogs incl. the 3 quoted camelCase tables.
- [ ] All queries typed from `database.types.ts`; failures go through `captureError`. `typecheck`/`lint`/`build` pass.

## Constraints
- No hand-written row types. No reimplementation of CNV/log-status/visibility. No ad-hoc SQL in components — it lives here. Respect the `app` schema targeting from the T02 client.

## Dependencies
- T02 (client/types), T05 (auth — JWT for RLS).

## Files Expected
- `src/lib/queries/leads.ts`, `clients.ts`, `refData.ts`
- `src/lib/rpc.ts` (extended)
- `src/lib/queries/keys.ts` (if using a cache)

tasks.description:
# Task 08 — Lead Detail View

> Read `build/prompts/_shared-context.md` first.

## Objective
Build the read-only Lead Detail view: a single lead's full summary with contact actions, entered from any lead-list chevron. Mirrors App-2.0 Screen 23, adapted to the `app` schema aggregate and the three audiences.

## Context
2.0 Screen 23 layout (top→bottom): status header card (log-status color + label + client name + submitted-by), contact row (Call/Message/Email icons), Edit Lead button (intake-only), Lead Info card (intake specialist, case manager, rep phone + "Call Rep"), Demographics, Treatment & Appointment, Attorney, Accident Notes, Multimedia, Comments thread. In 3.0 this reads the `getLead` aggregate (T07). Attorneys/affiliates also use this view (read-only) for leads RLS grants them.

## Technical Requirements
1. `src/pages/leads/LeadDetailPage.tsx` at `/leads/:idLead`. Load via `getLead(idLead)` (T07).
2. **Header card:** `StatusBadge` from `fn_log_status`/`lead.id_log_status`; client display name (primary `lead_party`→`client`); submitted-by (`app_user` via `submitter_user_id`) + created_at.
3. **Contact row:** Call/Message/Email actions on the primary client's `client_channel` values (tel:/sms:/mailto:). Use Capacitor-safe links.
4. **Edit Lead button:** visible only when `portalKind==='EMPLOYEE'`/ADMIN with intake capability (per role matrix); routes to Intake Panel (T10). Hidden/disabled for attorney/affiliate.
5. **Cards** (each from the aggregate, show "—" when null):
   - Lead Info: intake specialist + case manager (from `lead_staff` by `staff_kind`), rep phone + "Call Rep".
   - Demographics: client name, phone, address (`client_address`).
   - Treatment & Appointment: `lead_clinical` → `ref_tx_location` name, appointment_at, is_telemedicine.
   - Attorney: `lead_legal` → `ref_attorney` display_name, `refLegalStatus`, date_signed.

1. `src/pages/leads/NewLeadPage.tsx` (`/leads/new`) — single scrollable form, steps 2–5 locked until phone passes. EMPLOYEE/ADMIN only (guard).
2. **Phone gating:** debounced input → `findClientByPhone` / duplicate check against `app.client_channel` + `app.lead` (normalized phone) + format validity. Green banner on valid+unique; blocking error on duplicate/invalid. Block submit until passed.
3. **E5 structured validation** (`src/lib/validation/lead.ts`): reject empty/placeholder last names (".", ".."), emoji-in-name, DOB-embedded-in-name, duplicated first==last; clear inline errors. Use a schema (zod or equivalent).

Yes/No `PillToggle` (req, → `lead.boost_yn`); where client lives (state `Select`); accident state (`Select` from `ref_state`, req, → `lead_accident.id_accident_state`); passengers numeric (→ `lead_accident.passenger_count`). **Additional:** Language multi-`PillToggle` (→ `client.preferred_language` / notes); Notes textarea (→ `lead_note` type `accident`/`comment`). **Media:** upload images/files to a Supabase Storage bucket; associate refs.

7. Disable Submit while invalid/in-flight; success → navigate to the new lead's detail.

Ends with Lock Down (all fields complete → status→Locked Down) or Pending/Dropped/CNA. In 3.0 each section persists to its `app` summary table.

## Technical Requirements
1. `src/pages/leads/IntakePanelPage.tsx` (`/leads/:idLead/edit`). Guard: EMPLOYEE with intake capability or ADMIN (per role matrix); block others.
2. **Section → table mapping (persist per section):**
   - §1 Intake: accident date/type/location/fault/passengers → `lead_accident` (`date_of_accident`, `id_location_type`, `id_at_fault_type`, `passenger_count`); "Take Ownership" sets status CNA.
   - §2 Demographics: `client` (+`client_address`, `client_channel`) — First/Last/is_minor/DOB/phone(validated)/email/address/city/state/zip/language.
   - §3 Insurance: `lead_insurance` rows by `insurance_role` (PIP/AT_FAULT/PASSENGER) → `ref_insurance_carrier` (+`carrier_raw` when unmatched). Render boolean as Yes/No (fix 2.0 "false" bug).
   - §4 Injury & Damage: `lead_accident.id_property_severity`/`id_personal_severity` (rated `ref_severity_level`); injuries multi-select → `lead_injury_site` (from `ref_injury_site`); `lead_injury` flags.
   - §5 Treatment & Appointment: `lead_clinical` — `id_tx_location` (from `ref_tx_location`), `appointment_at`, `requires_transportation`, `is_telemedicine`.
   - §6 Attorney: `lead_legal` — `id_attorney` (from `ref_attorney`), prev-attorney?, police-report?, is_docusign, signing date, `id_legal_status`.
   - §7 Questionnaire (13 yes/no default No): map to `lead_accident`/`lead_injury` flags (ticket attorney, rideshare driver/passenger, fracture, ambulance, xray, mri, ct, hospital, commercial policy, construction, truck).
   - §8 Passengers: per-passenger `lead_party` (kind PASSENGER) with `party_sequence`, `client`, PIP `lead_insurance`, `id_tx_location`, appointment, personal injury; paginated; blocking validation.

4. **Lock Down flow:** when required fields complete, "Lock Down" sets stage/status Locked Down, writes `lead_timeline.date_locked_down`, records a `lead_status_event`. 5. Dropdowns from `refData` (T07). Save writes are per-section (autosave or explicit Save) with `captureError`. Recompute + store CNV/log-status via RPC after Lock Down.

- [ ] All 9 sections render and persist to the correct `app` summary tables per the mapping.
- [ ] Sequential gating enforced; passengers gated until §1–8 complete; per-passenger pagination works.
- [ ] Booleans render as Yes/No (not "false"); injuries multi-select persists to `lead_injury_site`.
- [ ] Lock Down / Pending / Dropped / CNA update status, write `lead_status_event`, and capture reasons; CNV + log-status recomputed via RPC.

> Read `build/prompts/_shared-context.md` first.

## Objective
Build the reusable charting infrastructure: Recharts donut+table wrappers and the server-side aggregation layer (Supabase RPC functions) that every dashboard uses. Establishes the App-2.0 "donut + data table" pattern once, cleanly, and moves aggregation to the database (premium bar: server-side aggregation over shipping large payloads).

## Context
2.0 charts are donut/ring + data table underneath (center total, teal gradient by rank, table sorted desc). Marketing/Intake/Atty charts (T17–T18) and Performance Roster (T19) all reuse this. Aggregations (New Leads, Locked Down, Came In, Signed, Dropped, LD-Dropped) must be computed in Postgres, scoped by RLS/hierarchy, not by fetching raw rows to the client.

## Technical Requirements
1. `src/features/charts/DonutTable.tsx` — presentational: takes `{ title, total, segments: {label, value}[] }`, renders a Recharts donut (center total, teal gradient by descending value) + a sorted `DataTable` (label + metric column, alternating rows). Reuse T03 `DonutChart`/`DataTable`.
2. **Aggregation RPCs** — add `migrations/0012_chart_rpcs.sql` (new migration; charts need server-side aggregation): SECURITY INVOKER functions that respect RLS, e.g.:
   - `app.agg_leads_by_metric(p_period text, p_metric text, p_group_by text)` → returns `(label, cnt)` grouped by rep/intaker/attorney/office/pod/team for a metric (new_leads, locked_down, came_in, signed, dropped, ld_dropped) over Today/MTD. Derive metrics from `lead` + `lead_timeline` + `lead_status_event` + `lead_org_snapshot`.
   - Keep them parameterized + indexed; document each in SCHEMA.md style comment. Apply + regenerate types.
3. `src/lib/queries/charts.ts` — typed wrappers over the RPCs; a `useChartData` hook with loading/empty/error.
4. **LEVEL/scope filter** support: functions accept a group_by dimension (Individual/Team/POD/Office/Region) and rely on RLS for row scope; the caller passes the chosen level.
5. Performance: measure RPC latency; ensure charts render from a single aggregated call (no N+1). Note timings in the PR.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `DonutTable` renders donut (center total, teal gradient) + sorted table from a segments array.

> Read `build/prompts/_shared-context.md` first.

## Objective

## Context
The critical correctness risks are: (1) an audience seeing another audience's data (RLS), (2) CNV/log-status computed wrong, (3) lead-creation/intake writing bad data. Tests must cover these explicitly.

## Technical Requirements
1. **Vitest unit** (`*.test.ts` colocated or in `tests/unit`):
   - Validation schema (T09 `lead.ts`): rejects placeholder/emoji/DOB-in-name; accepts valid input.
   - Intake section→payload mappers (T10): clinical + legal + insurance shape correctly.
   - Query builders / RPC wrappers: correct params to `fn_cnv_value`/`fn_log_status`/`agg_*` (mock supabase client).
   - Log-status/CNV wrappers return typed values.
2. **Playwright E2E** (`tests/e2e`) against a running app pointed at a test/staging Supabase (env-driven; document setup):
   - **Auth**: OTP login flow (mock/staging), unprovisioned-email state, sign-out.
   - **RLS visibility (critical)**: seed/login as EMPLOYEE, ATTORNEY, AFFILIATE (using the demo users) and assert each sees ONLY their scoped leads; assert an attorney cannot open another firm's lead URL (404/empty), same for affiliate/location.
   - **New Lead**: phone-gating blocks duplicate; happy path creates a lead in `app` and lands on detail.
   - **CNV**: the seeded confirmed+signed demo lead shows CNV 1.50.
3. Wire `test` (vitest) + `test:e2e` (playwright) scripts into CI (`ci-gate` runs `test`; e2e can be a separate job or `--if-present`). Provide fixtures/helpers for auth-as-role.
4. Coverage target: meaningful coverage on `lib/queries`, `lib/validation`, `lib/rpc`, auth, and portal guards (not a % vanity metric — the listed scenarios must exist and pass).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Vitest unit tests cover validation, intake mappers, and rule-engine wrappers; all pass.
- [ ] Playwright E2E covers auth, the three-audience RLS boundary (cross-audience denial), New Lead happy+duplicate, and CNV=1.50.
- [ ] `npm run test` passes in CI; e2e documented + runnable against staging.
- [ ] Cross-audience visibility test FAILS if RLS is weakened (proves it's real).

# Task 28 — Store Packaging (Signed iOS + Android + Metadata)

> Read `build/prompts/_shared-context.md` first.

## Objective
Produce build-and-package-ready, store-compliant signed artifacts — iOS `.ipa` and Android `.aab` — plus complete store metadata, so the app is ready for submission. **This task STOPS at signed artifacts + metadata handoff. It does NOT submit** (submission requires Jon's Apple Developer + Google Play accounts and explicit authorization).

## Context
Deliverable is "build-and-package-ready": compiling, store-guideline-compliant, signed artifact handoff — not actual submission. Signing credentials (Apple Developer $99/yr, Google Play $25) are provisioned by Jon; wire the pipeline to consume them from secrets/env, and document the exact steps.

## Technical Requirements
1. **Build config:** production `vite build` + `npx cap sync`; verify release configs for both platforms. Version/build numbers set (1.0.0 / 1).
2. **Android `.aab`:** Gradle release config, signing via a keystore supplied through env/secrets (NOT committed); produce a signed `.aab`. Document keystore generation + the CI secret names.
3. **iOS `.ipa`:** Xcode/`xcodebuild` archive + export config; signing via Apple Developer team/cert/provisioning supplied at build time (documented; requires a Mac — the pipeline documents/validates config, produces the archive step). Handle entitlements (push from T24), bundle id `com.tnfg.nofaultapp3`.
4. **Store guideline compliance:** privacy manifest / `NSUsageDescription` strings (camera/photos for media upload, notifications), Android permissions declared minimal, data-safety form content prepared, no private API use, offline/empty states OK, account-deletion/data-handling note (needed for both stores).
5. **Store metadata** (`store/` folder): app name, subtitle, description, keywords, category, screenshots (generated from key screens across device sizes), privacy policy URL placeholder, support URL, icon; both App Store + Play listings.
6. **Handoff doc** `store/HANDOFF.md`: exact steps + which secrets/accounts Jon must supply to sign + submit, and the final commands. Explicitly note: DO NOT submit without Jon's authorization.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Production build + `cap sync` succeed; version/build set; bundle id `com.tnfg.nofaultapp3`.
- [ ] Signed `.aab` produced via env-supplied keystore (or fully documented + validated if the signing secret is absent in CI); iOS archive/export config complete + documented.
- [ ] Privacy/permission/data-safety compliance content prepared for both stores.
- [ ] `store/` metadata + screenshots + `HANDOFF.md` complete.
- [ ] NO submission performed. `build`/`typecheck`/`lint`/`test` pass.

## Constraints
- **Do NOT submit to either store.** No certs/keystores/keys committed — all via secrets/env. Stop at signed-artifact + metadata handoff. Follow current Apple/Google guidelines.

- T25 (native integration), T26 (tests green), T27 (polish).

- `store/` (metadata, screenshots, listings), `store/HANDOFF.md`
